fact: The telecoms regulators of Burkina Faso, Mali (AMRTP) and Niger signed a cooperation convention creating the Conseil des regulateurs du Sahel, covering harmonised rules, free roaming, border spectrum coordination and joint positions in the ITU; the article gives no signing date, so its published date 2026-09-26 is used.
Mali's minister told the Council of Ministers that Mali took part in the 7th ordinary Plenipotentiary Conference of the African Telecommunications Union, held 23 to 24 July 2026 in Abuja.

At the ATU Plenipotentiary Conference in Abuja (23 to 24 July 2026) Mali was re-elected a member of the ATU Administrative Council for the 2027-2031 term; the communique gives no more exact election date.

Mali's Minister of Communication and Digital Economy met the Smart Africa Alliance director general on the sidelines of MWC 2026 in Barcelona and discussed skills, fibre links with neighbours and hosting the next Transform Africa Summit; talks only, no agreement signed.

Mali's digital minister took part in the opening of the fourth SIPEN-UEMOA digital economy fair in Ouagadougou and delivered the address on behalf of the AES Confederation's digital ministers; no agreement was signed, a Declaration of Ouagadougou was only anticipated.

Mali's government records that its minister for communication and digital economy took part in the signing at Ouagadougou of the Alliance des Etats du Sahel (AES) agreement on cross-border radio-frequency coordination, with the ministers of Niger and Burkina Faso.

fact: Ecofin Agency reports on 26 October 2026 that Mali reached roaming agreements with Benin and Togo in December 2023, and Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger signed an agreement under the Confederation of Sahel States in November 2024.
